source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    1. Check each boot option can boot normal after setting
  none  : Do not change boot device order
  pxe   : Force PXE boot
  disk  : Force boot from default Hard-drive
  diag  : Force boot from Diagnostic Partition
  cdrom : Force boot from CD/DVD
  bios  : Force boot into BIOS Setup
  floppy: Force boot from Floppy/primary removable media
2. All the device should be set.
3. To check boot settings by ipmitool command: ipmitool chassis bootparam get 5
4. To check BMC WEB 'Operations' > 'Server power operations' > Boot Settings override should matached with ipmitool setting.
5. Enable one time boot should be selected after setting.
6. Reboot and check the booting in next boot.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria:
1. Set ipmitool booting setting should be established successfully.
2. The one time boot should boot correctly after reboot.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis bootdev none 2>&1; ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -H "$BMC_IP" -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" chassis bootparam set bootflag force_bios 2>&1; echo ---; sshpass -p "$DUT_PASS" ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no $DUT_USER@$DUT_IP "cat /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id 2>&1"
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: set the next-boot option while the system is booted (e.g. force BIOS setup next boot), then reboot and confirm the setting took effect by reading the boot mode.
deepseek_columns.risk: RISK: state-changing: modifies the SUT next-boot setting (chassis bootdev) which alters the next OS boot; confirm the intended next device with the user first.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL recognizes the state-changing override but its command clears/sets `none` and then forces BIOS, covers only one of seven listed options, exposes credentials, disables SSH host verification, never actually reboots and treats an OS boot_id as boot-device proof.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED correctly requires a supported per-option matrix, complete IPMI/WebUI readback, reboot approval, console/device evidence and one-time-clear verification. V3.1 additionally separates set/readback, actual boot destination and second-boot reversion for every applicable option.
historical_reviews.round_02: Entry 912/2291 accepts command presence with generic preconditions but does not resolve `none`, unsupported legacy options, full parameter decoding, persistent versus one-time bits, real destination evidence or recovery between options.
historical_reviews.related_source_cases: The next Under Power off case tests setting the override while the host is off and is a separate power-state variant. Persistent boot-order and BMC WebUI-only UI cases are not substitutes.

historical_reviews.v3_1: ED-33 preserves all listed options and WebUI/IPMI comparison; ED-34 treats applicable devices, mappings and expected destination as Project inputs; ED-35 forbids reducing actual boot coverage to readback only; ED-38 requires approval per state change, recovery and no automatic retry.

original_test_intent: While the SUT is already booted, verify every Project-supported one-time next-boot option can be set, is represented consistently by IPMI and the BMC WebUI, selects the intended destination on the next approved reboot, then clears without changing persistent boot order.
original_method: For each applicable none, PXE, disk, diagnostic, CD/DVD, BIOS or floppy/removable option, baseline persistent order and override state, confirm the destination is present and safe, set exactly one one-time override, decode complete boot flags and WebUI state, reboot once after approval, prove the actual boot destination, then perform the required readback/normal-boot check before the next option.
manual_activity: An engineer approves the applicable option/destination matrix and every reboot. A human or trusted console observer confirms BIOS/diagnostic/removable destinations and performs recovery if a path is not bootable. Automation may set/read one approved override, compare WebUI/IPMI and collect boot evidence, but cannot authorize reboots or infer the verdict from boot_id.
required_inputs: BMC/SUT/BIOS/OS identities, verified booted state and persistent boot-order baseline
Applicable option matrix and exact IPMI/WebUI mapping including `none` semantics and unsupported-option expectation
Known safe PXE target, disk, diagnostic partition, optical/removable media, BIOS path and unique destination markers
Complete boot-parameter decoder and expected one-time/persistent flag encodings
Per-option reboot window, console/physical recovery, timeouts and second-boot reversion criteria
Secure credentials and verified host keys plus preserved audit/SEL/boot evidence plan
safety_requirements: Do not clear logs; preserve initial boot settings, persistent order, BMC audit/SEL and first-failure console evidence.
Verify target, current booted/power state and exact option before each write; never chain `none` and `force_bios` or advance automatically to another option.
Do not expose passwords with `-P`/sshpass, disable SSH host verification, or boot from an untrusted PXE server or removable image.
Obtain point-of-action approval for every override and reboot; perform one reboot only and stop on wrong destination, failed boot or console loss.
Do not alter persistent boot order. Decode all boot flags rather than trusting command success, UI label or an OS boot_id alone.
Clear/restore only the approved one-time state after evidence, verify normal policy on the next boot where required and retain local/console recovery.
agent_execution_scope: Validate identity, booted state, applicable option mapping, destination media, full flag decoder, persistent-order baseline, reboot approvals and recovery contract.
For one approved option at a time, set the one-time override through the selected method, re-read complete IPMI parameters and WebUI state and pause for reboot confirmation.
Collect BMC audit plus firmware/console/destination-specific evidence through reboot, then verify override consumption/clear and persistent-order integrity before any next option.
Stop without insecure authentication, untrusted media, log clear, blind retry, automatic matrix progression or DUT verdict.
engineer_actions: Approve applicable options, `none` semantics, exact interface mappings and unique boot-destination criteria.
Approve safe devices/PXE/media, each reboot and recovery/timeout/second-boot plan while protecting persistent order.
Review per-option set/readback/destination/clear evidence and issue formal verdicts.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Unfit as an executable matrix: it mixes clear and force-BIOS operations, omits reboot and most options, uses insecure authentication and reads only boot_id, which proves a reboot but not its source.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Generate one validated set/readback/reboot workflow per Project-supported option only after mappings and destinations are supplied. Use secure credentials and firmware/console/device-specific proof; do not chain options.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All seven source labels/descriptions, `bootparam get 5`, WebUI comparison, one-time selection, reboot Criteria, no Script, DeepSeek command/risk and 10/10-minute estimates remain preserved; Review does not assume all legacy devices exist.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Run an approved per-option state machine: baseline, one override write, complete IPMI/WebUI readback, one reboot, destination proof, consumption/clear and persistent-order comparison before proceeding.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: The selected BMC/IPMI/WebUI and BIOS boot implementation with provisioned safe destinations.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record BMC/IPMI/WebUI, BIOS/UEFI, OS, NIC/PXE and boot-media versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform IPMI boot-option mapping, BMC WebUI guide, BIOS boot policy and Project recovery plan.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds applicability, secure execution, destination-specific proof, clear/reversion and isolation between options while preserving the full matrix.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Readback alone does not prove boot; boot_id does not identify destination; testing only BIOS does not cover the remaining applicable options; an API override may not prove WebUI control.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Option map, destinations, flag decoder, approvals, evidence and recovery.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Bad or untrusted destinations can strand or compromise the host; legacy options may be unsupported; stale persistent flags can affect later boots.

project_override_considerations: A Project may use Redfish or a vendor tool instead of ipmitool if the source IPMI and WebUI requirements, actual method, reason, approval and field-equivalent mapping are recorded. Passing an override does not claim the omitted interface passed. Unsupported legacy options must be documented as not applicable from Project/platform authority, not silently skipped.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/booted-state identity, persistent boot-order and complete initial IPMI/WebUI boot-option baseline
Approved applicability and option-to-device/path matrix with trusted media/PXE identity and per-option recovery approval
Per-option write/audit, full decoded parameter 5 response, WebUI match and one-time/persistent flag state
Firmware/console and destination-specific proof for the next boot, not only boot_id, with timing and failure/recovery outcome
Post-boot consumption/clear, second normal-boot or equivalent reversion proof, unchanged persistent order, preserved logs and engineer-owned per-option verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Title, Procedure and Criteria consistently test one-time next-boot overrides from an already booted host. Vague `all device`, legacy-option applicability and `none` semantics require Project definition but do not create competing source purposes.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The one-time boot objective is clear. Project inputs can identify supported options, safe destinations, mappings and recovery. Missing data makes execution pending rather than the review permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Agrees on package classification and adds explicit under-booted precondition, per-option second-boot/reversion evidence and `none` semantics.

review_improvement: Prevents a clear-plus-force-BIOS command and kernel boot_id from being reported as complete seven-option coverage, and prevents an unapproved reboot or untrusted boot path from being launched automatically.
independent_technical_reasoning: A one-time boot override has three independently testable layers: requested flags, actual firmware destination and consumption/reversion after use. Command success covers only the first write. Platform option mappings and legacy device support vary, and `none` can mean clear rather than a boot target. Each applicable option therefore needs isolated readback, destination-specific evidence and post-boot clearing while preserving persistent order.
